🔒 Test locks Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock . Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects , while everything else keeps running in parallel: test ( 'update user settings' , { lock : 'user-settings' } , async ( { page } ) => { // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings' } ) ; A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock fo
